CHWC-Montpelier reported to CMS $1,305,874 in unreimbursed care (line 31 in cost report), of which $218,274 was charity care. Across all of Parkview Health’s 340B covered entities in Indiana, Parkview reported more than $143 million in unreimbursed care. Additionally, last year, Parkview Health partnered with Undue Medical Debt to abolish $64.13 million in debt for 35,694 patients.

CHWC-Montpelier participates in the 340B Drug Pricing Program and reinvests program savings to support access to care, improve clinical services, and reduce financial barriers for vulnerable and underserved patient populations. These investments are directed toward patient‑facing services and system capabilities that align with the program’s statutory intent.
Subsidized health services at CHWC-Montpelier include ambulance/EMS, hospice, outpatient rehab, neonatology, and other services.

Community benefit investments (as reported on IRS form 990 schedule H 2024) across all of Parkview Health’s 340B covered entities in Indiana surpassed $36 million for community health services that are not billed - Examples across Parkview Health include childbirth classes, postpartum support, diabetes education, mobile health services, cystic fibrosis intervention, blood pressure clinics, and additional services.

Savings are also reinvested at Parkview Health in a broad range of clinical services that improve quality, safety, and continuity of care. These include acute and outpatient clinical services, chronic disease management programs, outpatient infusion services, and pharmacist‑led programs such as medication therapy management, prior authorization support, immunization programs, and antibiotic stewardship. Parkview also supports preventive care, community wellness initiatives, and behavioral health services. Research and innovation programs are included to advance care delivery and outcomes.

Parkview uses 340B savings to directly reduce patient out‑of‑pocket costs and support medication affordability. This includes a robust pharmacy-managed, means-tested patient assistance program. This is intended to promote medication adherence and continuity of care for financially vulnerable patients.

Savings are also applied to provider education initiatives, including physician, nursing, and pharmacy training programs, to support a well‑prepared healthcare workforce capable of delivering high‑quality, patient‑centered care.
